Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced a simultaneous price increase for Apple TV+. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the Apple TV+ monthly fee will rise from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

Apple One's Individual plan has also been similarly hiked.

Apple TV+ and Apple One both go up in price

Below are the full details of this price increase:

  • Apple TV+ (monthly): US$14.99 (originally US$12.99)
  • Apple TV+ (annual): US$119 (originally US$99)
  • Apple One Individual: US$21.95 (originally US$19.95)

Prices for other Apple One plans remain unchanged. Last month, when Apple raised the price of Apple Music, it also raised the monthly fees for Apple One Family and Apple One Premier, but did not raise the Individual plan.

The new fees apply to new subscribers starting today. Apple says existing subscribers will receive a price increase notice about a month before being charged the new price.

The last time Apple raised the Apple TV+ price was in August 2025, when the monthly fee was lowered from US$12.99 to US$9.99. At that time, Apple did not adjust the annual plan or the Apple One bundle pricing.

Over the past year, Apple has significantly expanded the Apple TV+ content lineup. Last October, Apple announced a deal with Formula 1 (F1), becoming F1's exclusive broadcast partner in the United States. The F1 streaming service is included in a standard Apple TV+ subscription at no extra cost.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) match streaming to Apple TV+, likewise at no extra cost. Previously, watching MLS required a separate subscription to MLS Season Pass.

Apple is also buoyed now by the success of recent additions such as the fourth season of Ted Lasso. As of today, Apple TV+ is airing season two of Dark Matter; the sixth season of Slow Horses will premiere on 16 September.

What do you think of the new Apple TV+ pricing? Is US$14.99 a reasonable price for what Apple TV+ offers? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
